subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Arch Bridges: Pushing Sideways to Stay Up
description: Learn Arch Bridges: Pushing Sideways to Stay Up in one minute.

hook.text: The Pont du Gard in France has carried water and traffic for 2,000 years. It's a stone arch bridge.

buildup.text: Arch bridges convert vertical loads into horizontal thrust. The arch pushes outward against its supports.

discovery.text: Stone and concrete are perfect for arches because they excel in compression. No steel needed.

twist.text: During construction, arches need temporary wooden frames called centering. Remove them too early and everything falls.

climax.text: Modern arch bridges span over 500 meters. China's Beipanjiang bridge arches across a 565-meter canyon.

punchline.text: The arch doesn't fight gravity. It redirects it.

quiz.question: How does an arch bridge handle vertical loads?
options: It absorbs them into flexible cables above the deck
It converts them into horizontal thrust against supports
It transfers them directly to the riverbed below
